result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both emails clearly state the date, price, card charge and Settings > Billing cancel path, and both describe the 60-day read-only period and CSV export without using deletion as a threat. B says the paid plan keeps unlimited invoices, which the facts don't support, and promises a reply from a person, which also wasn't given; A flags the unlimited-invoices gap instead of guessing. B's note that Nov 9, 2026 is a Monday is a useful catch, but A sticks to the supplied facts better and its preview text puts the price and cancel path up front. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both emails clearly give the date, the $12 charge to the card on file, the Settings > Billing cancel path and the 60-day read-only period with CSV export, without pressure. Answer A says the paid plan keeps unlimited invoices, but the facts only say the trial includes them. Answer B avoids that claim and flags the gap. A usefully notes that Nov 9, 2026 is a Monday, but that does not outweigh the invented claim in the email itself.
